Q1: Which fix should this issue ship, given that its own constraints say "a retry, backoff, re-run, or longer timeout is not an accepted fix"?
Choices:
A) Allow the bounded client retry anyway. The cause is that a temporary "could not verify" 403 is read as a final refusal. In `scripts/claude_pool_token.sh`, retry the broker call at most 3 times, using the existing `oidc_retry_sleeps` intervals and `oidc_retry_on` switch. Retry only on `000`, `429`, `5xx`, or `403` with `workflow_sha_unverifiable`; every other 403 reason still fails at once. The regression test in `tests/test_claude_pool_token.py` sends one `403 workflow_sha_unverifiable` and then a 200. It fails on the current head and passes with the fix. (RECOMMENDED)
B) No client retry. Ship only the broker change: when the `main` check is `unavailable`, still check `stable`, and grant if either says yes. **Note:** this needs Q2:B. Selecting it with Q2:A leaves nothing in scope to change.
C) Both the client retry (A) and the broker change (B). **Note:** this needs Q2:B.
Q2: Should this PR edit the broker files under `tools/claude-pool-broker/`?
Choices:
A) No. Keep to the heal-scope allowlist: `scripts/claude_pool_token.sh`, `tests/**` and a `changelog.d/*.md` entry. Leave the broker code and its stale "job runs codex" comments to #9990 / PR #9995, which already edits those files, and list them in the PR body as follow-ups. Note in the PR body that an operator needs to confirm `BROKER_GITHUB_READ_TOKEN` is set on the Worker. (RECOMMENDED)
B) Yes. Widen scope to `tools/claude-pool-broker/src/index.ts` (the `verifyTrustedSha` change and the header comment), `wrangler.toml` (the comment) and `tools/claude-pool-broker/test/broker.test.ts`. This may conflict with PR #9995. The Worker change only takes effect once someone redeploys the Worker, because no workflow deploys it.
